question.text: Under SEBI regulations, upfront commission from AMCs to mutual fund distributors has been largely abolished and the framework is now trail-only. What is the primary regulatory concern that this addresses?

answer.text: Upfront commissions were too expensive for AMCs and reduced their profitability
Upfront commissions created a conflicted incentive that could lead to mis-selling, including over-transacting or churning to earn higher commissions
Upfront commissions were being paid from investor capital, reducing the NAV at the time of purchase
Upfront commissions violated the AMFI code of conduct regarding maximum compensation limits

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook explains that the current framework is trail-only, with no upfront commission and no upfronting of trail commission. This SEBI provision is aimed at discouraging mis-selling driven by upfront-payout incentives. The AMFI code separately prohibits over-transacting and churning to earn higher commissions, so churning is one example of the broader conflicted-incentive concern. The Trap: Option A frames it as an AMC profitability issue; the rationale is investor protection. Option C is mechanically inaccurate for the current framework. Option D invents a specific AMFI rule that is not the regulatory driver. Note: The shift to trail-only commission aligns distributor incentives with long-term investor outcomes — the distributor earns more as the investor stays invested and the AUM grows.
